main.title: 3D television enters the living room
main.subtitle: Depth through two different images
main.summary: In 2010, consumer 3D televisions brought stereoscopic films and games into the home through compatible screens, content and glasses.

cards.heading: Depth through two different images
cards.text: Major television manufacturers promoted stereoscopic home viewing in 2010. Sony's BRAVIA range paired high-refresh-rate screens with active-shutter glasses, showing different images to the left and right eyes to create depth. Some models included the glasses and transmitter; others required separate accessories. Compatible films, players and broadcasts completed the setup. Sony also announced PlayStation 3 updates for stereoscopic games and Blu-ray 3D playback, extending the format across television, cinema releases and games.

main.title: iPad
main.summary: Apple unveiled its first iPad on January 27, 2010: a tablet with a 9.7-inch touchscreen, an A4 processor and downloadable apps.

cards.heading: iPad
cards.text:
Apple unveiled the first iPad on January 27, 2010, at an event presented by Steve Jobs. The tablet combined an Apple A4 processor with a 9.7-inch touchscreen. Its software supported web browsing, email and music, with downloadable apps adding games, reference tools, navigation and other services. Some models also connected to cellular networks.

The Wi-Fi model reached US stores on April 3, followed by the Wi-Fi + 3G version on April 30. International sales began on May 28 in Australia, Canada, France, Japan, Italy, Germany, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

main.title: Inception
main.summary: Inception is Christopher Nolan's 2010 science-fiction heist film about a thief entering dreams to steal information or implant an idea.

cards.heading: Inception
cards.text:
Inception is Christopher Nolan's 2010 science-fiction heist film, produced with Emma Thomas. Leonardo DiCaprio plays a thief who enters his targets' subconscious to steal information. He is offered a chance to erase his criminal record by performing the reverse task: implanting an idea. The cast includes Ken Watanabe, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Marion Cotillard, Elliot Page, Tom Hardy, Cillian Murphy, Tom Berenger, Dileep Rao and Michael Caine.

Nolan first presented Warner Bros. with an eighty-page treatment about dream thieves after completing Insomnia in 2002. He set it aside while making Batman Begins, The Prestige and The Dark Knight, then revised it over six months. Warner Bros. bought the treatment in February 2009. Filming spanned six countries, beginning in Tokyo in June and ending in Canada in November, with a budget of US$160 million.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 1
main.subtitle: The final journey leaves the classroom behind
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 1 takes Harry, Ron and Hermione away from the timetable and shelter of Hogwarts. They search for Horcruxes while moving between temporary hiding places, uncertain leads and a wizarding world increasingly controlled by Voldemort's followers. David Yates directs the first half of the final novel, released on 19 November 2010. Without teachers regularly supplying answers, the three friends have to make decisions together, and the exhaustion of their journey begins to strain the relationships that have carried them this far.

cards.heading: Three friends on the run
cards.text: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 1 takes Harry, Ron and Hermione away from the timetable and shelter of Hogwarts. Without teachers regularly supplying answers, the three friends have to make decisions together, and the exhaustion of their journey begins to strain the relationships that have carried them this far.

cards.heading: A story within the story
cards.text: An animated interlude gives a different visual form to one of the clues. As Hermione reads The Tale of the Three Brothers, figures and landscapes unfold in a stylised world built around shadows and puppet-like movement. Ben Hibon directed the sequence, created by Framestore, to make the folktale a distinct story inside the live-action film. Its objects and choices then become part of the larger search. Alexandre Desplat's score introduces the unsettled journey through Obliviate, while the film leaves its conflict open for the second part to resolve.

main.title: Arab Spring
main.summary: The Arab Spring (Arabic: الربيع العربي, romanized: ar-rabīʻ al-ʻarabī) was a series of pro-democracy anti-government protests, uprisings, and armed rebellions that spread across much of the Arab world in the early 2010s.

cards.heading: Arab Spring
cards.text: The Arab Spring (Arabic: الربيع العربي, romanized: ar-rabīʻ al-ʻarabī) was a series of pro-democracy anti-government protests, uprisings, and armed rebellions that spread across much of the Arab world in the early 2010s. It began in Tunisia in response to the death of Mohamed Bouazizi by self-immolation. From Tunisia, the protests initially spread to five other countries: Libya, Egypt, Yemen, Syria and Bahrain. The rulers deposed include: Zine El Abidine Ben Ali of Tunisia, Muammar Gaddafi of Libya, and Hosni Mubarak of Egypt, all in 2011; and Ali Abdullah Saleh of Yemen in 2012. Major uprisings and social violence occurred, including riots, civil wars, or insurgencies. Sustained street demonstrations took place in Morocco, Iraq, Algeria, Lebanon, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman and Sudan. Minor protests took place in Djibouti, Mauritania, Palestine, Saudi Arabia and the Western Sahara. A major slogan of the demonstrators in the Arab world is ash-shaʻb yurīd isqāṭ an-niẓām! (Arabic: الشعب يريد إسقاط النظام, lit. 'the people want to bring down the regime').

main.title: Fukushima nuclear accident
main.summary: The earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 triggered a major accident at Japan's Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power station.

cards.heading: Fukushima nuclear accident
cards.text: The earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 triggered a major accident at Japan's Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power station. The disaster interrupted the electrical supply and damaged almost all backup power sources. Reactors had shut down, but the loss of sufficient cooling led to containment failures and radioactive releases into the surrounding environment. Workers faced radiation exposure and physical injuries while responding. The United Nations scientific committee described it as the worst nuclear incident since Chernobyl. The sequence showed how damage to power and cooling systems could continue threatening reactors after shutdown.

main.title: Game of Thrones
main.subtitle: A struggle for the throne reaches across families and continents
main.summary: Game of Thrones brings George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novels to television through several competing families. Created for the screen by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss, the HBO series premiered in the United States on 17 April 2011. The first season sends Ned Stark toward royal power while his family and other claimants face dangers far from the capital.

cards.heading: Families in a contested kingdom
cards.text: Game of Thrones brings George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novels to television through several competing families. Created for the screen by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss, the HBO series premiered in the United States on 17 April 2011. The first season sends Ned Stark toward royal power while his family and other claimants face dangers far from the capital.

cards.heading: The reach of a promise
cards.text: The story moves between courts, households, military camps and distant borders. A promise made in one place can alter the prospects of people who have never met the speaker. This structure makes inheritance, marriage and political loyalty practical forces in the plot. The audience follows characters with incompatible goals, so success for one household may be a catastrophe for another. Familiarity with a central figure offers little certainty about what the struggle will cost them.

cards.heading: A world beyond the capital
cards.text: The opening titles turn geography into part of the viewing experience, guiding attention across an expanding world. Large settings and battles share space with private negotiations whose consequences may be equally severe. As the series develops, the return of supernatural threats places the contest for immediate power against dangers that require cooperation. Its ensemble form makes that tension persistent: characters can understand a crisis and still find their local obligations stronger than the case for a common response.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 is a 2011 epic fantasy film directed by David Yates from a screenplay by Steve Kloves.

cards.heading: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2
cards.text:
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 is a 2011 epic fantasy film directed by David Yates from a screenplay by Steve Kloves. It is the second of two cinematic parts based on the 2007 novel by J. K. Rowling, and the eighth and final instalment of the Harry Potter film series. The film follows Harry as he continues his quest to find and destroy Lord Voldemort's Horcruxes in order to destroy him once and for all.

The film stars an ensemble cast comprising Daniel Radcliffe as Harry Potter, and Rupert Grint and Emma Watson as Harry's best friends, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, alongside Helena Bonham Carter, Robbie Coltrane, Warwick Davis, Ralph Fiennes, Michael Gambon, John Hurt, Jason Isaacs, Gary Oldman, Alan Rickman, Maggie Smith, David Thewlis, and Julie Walters. Principal photography began on 19 February 2009, and was completed on 12 June 2010, with reshoots taking place in December 2010.

main.title: Occupy Wall Street
main.summary: Occupy Wall Street began in New York's Zuccotti Park on 17 September 2011.

cards.heading: Occupy Wall Street
cards.text: Occupy Wall Street began in New York's Zuccotti Park on 17 September 2011. Protesters opposed economic inequality, the power of finance and the influence of money in politics. Their occupation of the Financial District park lasted fifty-nine days, until 15 November. Anger drew partly on the aftermath of the Great Recession and taxpayer-funded rescues of financial institutions. The movement also challenged rules allowing corporations to spend freely on independent political campaigns. Gathering near Wall Street gave those concerns a visible setting at the centre of American finance.

main.title: Higgs boson
main.summary: The discovery of the Higgs boson was announced at the Large Hadron Collider in 2012, providing evidence for a particle associated with the Higgs field.

cards.heading: Higgs boson
cards.text:
The discovery of the Higgs boson was announced at the Large Hadron Collider in 2012. The particle is an excitation of the Higgs field, a component of the Standard Model of particle physics. Interactions with that field give elementary particles their mass.

The boson has zero spin and no electric or colour charge. It is highly unstable, decaying into other particles almost immediately after it is produced. The discovery connected an observed particle to a field whose role had been developed within the theory of fundamental interactions.
